text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Killing elephants for ivory urged: Species no longer endangered, African nations say, and harvest would curb poaching.
- Canadians prefer missing the bus: Public-transit use in steady decline.
- Bran products seek cancer-fighter label: Kellogg's bid could aid muffin makers.
- Election does little to stem separatism.
- War suspect's family denies intimidation: Potential witnesses questioned before Canadian court starts hearings in Ukraine.
- Ex-Bay boss to lead Eaton's: Kosich surprises observers by resurfacing as CEO of troubled department store chain.
- CIBC profit lower than Street's expectations: Shortfall attributed to weak markets, increased spending.
- Acklands unit in Chapter 11: Victim of cutthroat U.S. parts business.
- Diamond miners remove staff from Sierra Leone.
- Ex-Bay boss to head Eaton's: Troubled retailer thinks of the Bay and picks George Kosich for top spot - only the third time someone outside the family has held the job.
- McWatters and underwriters in wrangle over gold reserves.
